title: Taking a Replacement Item in Place of Money on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Return
content:
Where a customer asks to take a replacement item instead of money back on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking return, that acceptance is put on the return as an exchange. The result the exchange governs is the difference coming back to the customer on the swap. An exchange is offered on the schedules that allow one and inside the schedule's exchange window, counted in calendar days from the day the item was delivered as day zero, to which the window extension days of the tier the membership stood on when the return was asked for are added where the schedule takes the member extension. The difference returned on an exchange is fixed only after the relief the membership allows against the restocking fee owed on the return stands recorded against that return with the membership as its ground.

Recording the exchange adds an entry to the return's history naming the stock number going out to the customer, an exchange order reference the retailer issues for it and the difference being returned on the swap, and marks the return as taking a replacement rather than money. From that moment the customer can see that they have taken the replacement rather than the money, and what is coming back to them alongside it.

## Taking the acceptance

The acceptance is taken with `accept_exchange_item_1cf629c9`, which is a tool of the customer's own: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it. Only the customer may accept an exchange, since it disposes of what they are owed on the return.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `return_authorization_id` | the reference number of the return authorisation being settled by the swap, read from the return authorisation record retrieved for the customer before the call |
| `price_difference_amount` | the difference coming back to the customer on the swap, in USD to 2 decimal places, never negative, given to the cent with at most two decimal places and never carrying a currency symbol or thousands separator; 0.00 where nothing comes back |
| `exchange_sku` | the stock number of the item going out to the customer, copied character for character from the stock number shown on the return authorisation record, preserving its wording, digits, letters, case and punctuation exactly, with no translation, normalisation, summarising, addition or deletion |

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the exchange entry reference that was created, the stock number going out, the exchange order reference issued for it and the difference returned in USD to two decimal places. The sentence appearing at all means the exchange was recorded against the return.
